title: Sudoku: Scanning Rows, Columns and Boxes
subject: thinking

sections.body: A 6 by 6 Sudoku uses the numbers 1 to 6. The boxes are 2 squares tall and 3 squares wide. Each row, column and box holds each number once.
Scanning means looking along a row, a column and a box to see which numbers are already there. A number you can see cannot go in the empty square.
Example: an empty square has 1, 3 and 5 in its row, 2 and 6 in its column and 3 in its box. Put all of those together: 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6. Only 4 is not in the list, so the square is 4.
A good habit: start with the row, column or box that has the most numbers. It has the fewest empty squares, so there are fewer choices.
Take a 6 by 6 puzzle. Pick the row with the most numbers in it. Write which numbers are missing, then look at each empty square's column for clues.

Scanning is the first real technique in Sudoku. Ask 'what can I see in the row, in the column and in the box?' before every guess. Guessing is not needed: every puzzle in the app has exactly one solution that logic can find.

quiz.q: A 6 by 6 row has 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6. One square is empty. Which number goes there?
hints: A row holds 1 to 6 once each.
Which of the numbers 1 to 6 is not in the row?
Example: a row with 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 is missing 1. Find the missing number for 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6.
quiz.explain: The row has 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6. The missing number is 3.

quiz.q: An empty square has 1, 3 and 5 in its row, 2 and 6 in its column and 3 in its box. Which number can go there?
hints: Put together every number you can see in the row, column and box.
You can see 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6. Which number from 1 to 6 is left?
Example: row 1, 2, column 4, box 2, 3 leaves 5 and 6, so two numbers are still possible. Do the same with the numbers in this question.
quiz.explain: The numbers you can see are 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6. Only 4 is left.

quiz.q: Why is it a good idea to start with the row, column or box that has the most numbers already?
options: It has the fewest empty squares, so fewer choices
It is the quickest line to draw, so it saves time
It always starts with the number 1, so it is easy
hints: Think about how many squares are still empty there.
Fewer empty squares means fewer numbers that could go in them.
Example: a row with five numbers has only one empty square, so you know what goes in it at once. Compare that with a row that has only one number.
quiz.explain: A full line has few empty squares left, so there are fewer possible numbers and you find the answer faster.
